recipes.name: Macaroni and Cheese with Caramelized Onions and Bacon

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook elbow macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, for 8 minutes (noodles will still be slightly hard). Drain. Transfer to a large bowl; add 4 tablespoons butter and toss to coat.
Whisk sour cream, cream cheese, and egg together; stir into macaroni. Stir in 3 cups each Asiago cheese and Cheddar cheese.

Cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Reserve drippings in skillet. Transfer bacon to a paper towel-lined plate to drain, then chop into small pieces.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Add onion, 2 tablespoons butter, and garlic to drippings; cook and stir over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add brown sugar; cook, stirring occasionally, until onion very soft and golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes. Stir in bacon, parsley, and panko bread crumbs; transfer to a small bowl and set topping aside.

Heat same skillet over medium-low heat. Add remaining 2 tablespoons butter; melt. Whisk in flour; stir until light golden brown and becomes paste-like, about 5 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook and stir until smooth and thickened. Stir in hot pepper sauce, ground mustard, paprika, pepper, and salt. Remove sauce from heat; let cool 5 minutes.
Pour sauce over macaroni mixture, stir to coat. Transfer to the prepared baking dish; sprinkle with remaining 1 cup each Asiago cheese and Cheddar cheese. Top with bread crumb topping.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot, bubbling, and golden brown on top, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Macaroni and Cheese with Caramelized Onions and Bacon
raw_recipe.description: This rich and creamy casserole is packed full of gooey cheese and topped with crispy bacon and onion breadcrumbs.

video.description: The only thing that can possibly make mac ‘n’ cheese better than it already is bacon, right? How about caramelized onions and a crunchy topping, too? Mix buttered cooked macaroni with sour cream, egg, cream cheese, grated Asiago and Cheddar cheeses. After cooking bacon, add butter, onion and garlic to the drippings, then add brown sugar and onions and after softened, add bacon, parsley and panko bread crumbs. Create a sauce of butter, milk, mustard, paprika, salt, pepper and hot sauce. Layer everything in a baking dish and bake a dish everyone will be on time to the table for!

review.reviewBody: I thought this recipe was deliciuous! My family loved it! The only thing I would do differently the next time I make it is double the bacon and bread crumbs. That sweet crunchy topping was wonderul and I wanted more!

This is sooo good. I halved the recipe so it would fit in my 3 Qt. Pyrex dish. I used a combination of extra sharp cheddar and Emmentaler Swiss because that's what I had on hand. I did not have sour cream or creamed cheese but it still came out silky smooth and delicious. Followed the rest of the recipe. No matter what mac & cheese recipe you use try this topping....amazing. I doubled the bacon of course and the topping took this Mac & Cheese to the next level.

Sooooo unhealthy! But yummy. So, we prepare this once every couple of months. I cut way back on the butter (I only use 2 T in the pasta and skip the rest in favor of the bacon fat). 

You can make this ahead of time and keep in the fridge over night (I do this). I also bake it in a disposable pan to keep the mess down to a minimum.

Woo-hoo! this is YUMMY! I did take suggestions and doubled the topping part but I used 1/2 red onion and 1/2 diced sweet baby peppers. I also mixed about 3/4 of the topping into the pasta and cheese and used the remaining mixture for the top. I only had about 6 c. total grated cheese (Asiago and medium cheddar) so I sprinkled grated parm on the top before putting the remaining topping on. This did take quite a while to prep--about 1-1/2 hrs. I measured out all of the ingredients first and made sure to let everything get to room temperature. I also combined a few steps by snipping the bacon into pieces before cooking and then I added the onion, peppers & garlic when the bacon was almost done. I removed this mix to paper towels and patted extra grease off. In the same pan (NOT a non-stick!) I did still add the 2 T. of butter before making the rue/sauce, making sure to scrape all of the bacony goodness when whisking. It's a fair amount of work but totally delicious! I am loving the cheddar/Asiago/Parmesean combo.

Tripled the panko. Doubled the bacon. Carmelized the onions naturally over a 2-hour period without brown sugar. Used red pepper flakes instead of hot sauce.

OMG. So perfectly complex and delicious. Prep time was nowhere near 20 mins. All told, it took about 1:45 to make.

Made a half recipe as there are only three of us. Did the carmalaized onions in the crock pot so cut down on time to make the dish. It was amazing...will make again as a whole recipe for Easter or when I have a large group. EVERYONE loved it! I did double the topping as suggested and glad I did.

I added ricotta cheese to the cream cheese mixture, cooked the bacon in the oven at 400 degrees for about 35 minutes flipping halfway which made things a lot easier. This is the ultimate comfort food.

This recipe is fabulous! This has a lot of steps and takes a bit of time, but of so worth it! It was all the rave at our Thanksgiving feast! As per other reviews, I doubled the topping and used 3 cups each asiago & extra sharp white cheddar - divided. Will definitely make again!
This was really tasty! I used sharp white cheddar, asiago, and smoked gouda cheeses. Doubled the bacon and bread crumb topping...DELICIOUS!!

I made it with 1/2 the cheese and no paprika, but I prepared it for 50 co-workers and am playing it safe with the spice (and I didn't want to pay $20 on cheese, ha). I used mostly sharp cheddar with some high-quality Parmesan I had in the fridge. I also made twice the bacon, because everyone (except my weird, but super awesome, 11-year-old son) loves more bacon. 

THE GRAVY IS BRILLIANT, and I will be making it with sausage and adding it to homemade biscuits. (Oh, yes. I noticed.)

Please rename this "Dreamy Mac n' Cheese" ...Seriously. 

LOL at the people who said this took too long. Because, it's so worth it. It took me almost 3 hours...WORTH IT! 5 STARS, MY COOKING CHAMPIONS!
An adult version of the comfort food! It has a very gourmet taste when Asiago cheese was used! This is the third time that I made the recipe already!! Loved the taste and look of the dish!

Well, I didn't think I would ever taste a Mac n Cheese dish that stood apart from every other recipe but here we are. Mid recipe I was really skeptical regarding how this dish would come out but it is incredibly creamy, has a wonderful smokey, cheesy flavor profile and the topping was such an ingenious addition to a classic dish with an evolving flavor profile with every bite. I didn't change a thing (as I'm apt to do) and I'm pleased that I didn't. Easy to make and a winning dish! Can't take a photo because it was dished out and disappeared that fast.

I'm not a lazy cook (well, most of the time!). BUT, the end product must be worth the effort and this dish was not IMO. Flavor was good - how can you go wrong with THOSE ingredients? What disappointed me was the dryness. Too much pasta? Baked too long? I used pre-cooked (real) bacon so maybe it needed that extra grease? It's not a cheap dish with all that fancy cheese so that plus the amount of work required, won't be making again.
Great to have ready before appts. then just bake when you get home and have guests coming.

This recipe is A LOT OF WORK, but the finished product is amazing. We have made this a few times. Definitely a lot of prep time, so we don't make it often, only for a special occasion. Excellent mac and cheese, the topping makes it the best we've ever tasted.
I made this recipe three years in a row. My family loves it. I definitely recommend it. Yum.

I have made this numerous times and, while I am not the main cook in the family, this is one of our favorite meals! Today is my daughter's birthday, and this recipe is what she wants for her birthday dinner! Can't say enough about it...! An effort to make, but well worth it!!!

This is my family's favorite macaroni and cheese dish! I have made this recipe many times and it is always requested from my children that are now adults. I don't change much. Sometimes I don't use the cream cheese cuz it's a little rich but I do everything like the recipe says.

The best Mac n chz on the planet, I've made this at least a dozen times. It takes a while to prep and I only make it on holidays but I have it ready the night before so I can just take it from the fridge and throw it in the oven the next day. I also make double the topping, the topping is the best and you want some in every bite!
The only drawback to this dish is that I cannot take credit for it. I am looking forward to making a double batch and bringing it to the next big family event. Aloha
